candidates.exact_span: Pollutant Table (2 or 3) appropriate for permittee's land application practices.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Table 2 (loading-rate limits) or Table 3 (concentration criteria) governs determines which enforceable numeric limits apply for comparison (A) and which pollutant-reporting schema is required (B).

candidates.exact_span: The frequency of monitoring listed in Element 1, Section I.C. which applies to the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The cross-referenced monitoring frequency and the phrase 'which applies to the permittee' determine which monitoring intervals were obligatory; a different reading changes whether expected results are missing versus not required (C).

Pass/Fail reporting is qualitatively different from numeric mg/kg limits; interpretation affects whether an enforceable numeric discharge limit exists for comparison (A) versus a report-only or categorical compliance test (B).

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/Kg) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 1 (defined as a monthly average) as well as the applicable pollutant concentration criteria (mg/K g) listed in Table 3 found in Element 1, Section III, or the applicable pollutant loading rate limit (kg/ha) listed in Table 2 above if it exceeds 90% of the limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This clause ties reported values to Table 3 concentration criteria or, conditionally, Table 2 loading-rate limits at a 90% threshold, and defines the monitoring period as a monthly average; different readings change which limit applies, when loading-rate comparison is operative, and whether absent loading-rate data reflects non-requirement or missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Level of pathogen reduction achieved (C lass A or Class B).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Class A versus Class B status gates downstream conditional reporting (e.g., site restrictions in item f) and Section III applicability; misclassification changes which monitoring obligations were in force and how to classify unreported pathogen data.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative used as listed in Section I.B.3.(a. or b.). Alternatives describe how the pathogen reduction requirements are met. If Class B sludge, include information on how site restrictions were met in the DMR comment section or attach a separate sheet to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The cross-reference to Section I.B.3 alternatives and the Class B-only site-restriction reporting condition determine whether additional monitoring/documentation was required; interpretation affects obligation applicability (B) and whether missing restriction evidence is a gap or inapplicable (C).

candidates.exact_span: Vector attraction reduction alternative used as listed in Section I.B.4. h.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which vector-attraction alternative applies (via Section I.B.4) determines whether a separate vector-reduction reporting obligation was triggered for the permittee.

candidates.exact_span: When the amount of any pollutant applied to the land exceeds 90% of the cumulative pollutant loading rate for that pollutant, as described in Table 2, the permittee shall report the following information as an attachment to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 90% cumulative-loading trigger activates supplemental reporting and ties compliance assessment to Table 2 loading rates; different interpretations of 'amount applied' or the threshold change when loading-rate limits become operative for evaluation (A), what extra monitoring/reporting was required (B), and how to treat periods without attachment data (C).

candidates.locator: page 10, part_i, item l, bullet on cumulative pollutant
candidates.exact_span: The cumulative amount of each pollutant (i.e., kilograms/hectare) listed in Table 2 in the bulk sewage sludge applied to each site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Site-specific cumulative kg/ha reporting is the evidentiary basis for comparing applied loading against Table 2 limits; interpretation of cumulative accounting scope affects limit-exceedance evaluation (A) and whether site-level monitoring was required once thresholds were approached (B).

candidates.locator: page 10, part_i, item l, certification bullet
candidates.exact_span: I certify, under penalty of law, that the information that will be used to determine compliance with the requirements to obtain information in 40 CFR 503.12(e)(2) have been met for each site on which bulk sewage sludge is applied. This determination has been made under my direction and supervision in accordance with the system designed to ensure that qualified personnel properly gather and evaluate the information used to determine that the requirements to obtain information have been met. I am aware that there are significant penalties for false certification including fine and imprisonment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The certification ties DMR attachments to 40 CFR 503.12(e)(2) information-obtaining requirements; whether this satisfies or substitutes for underlying monitoring evidence affects what obligations were met (B) and whether missing numeric results are documented no-data versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.locator: page 10, part_i, item l, final bullet
candidates.exact_span: A description of how the requirements to obtain information in 40 CFR 503.12(e)(2) are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This descriptive requirement defines what constitutes adequate documentation when cumulative loading thresholds are exceeded; interpretation determines whether monitoring was required beyond ordinary DMR parameters and how to classify absent descriptions.

candidates.locator: page 10, Section III, opening applicability paragraph
candidates.exact_span: For those permittees with sludge that contains concentrations of pollutants below those pollutant limits listed in Table 3 for bulk or bagged (containerized) sewage sludge and also meet the Class A pathogen reduction requirements, the following conditions apply (Note: All bagged sewage sludge must be treated by Class A pathogen reduction requirements.):
candidates.computation_change_reason: This conditional applicability gate determines whether Section III (Table 3 concentration-based) requirements bind a given permittee; different readings of 'below those pollutant limits' or simultaneous Class A satisfaction change which numeric limits and monitoring rules apply (A,B) and whether missing Section III data is inapplicable versus unresolved (C).
